page: Microsoft Azure D32plds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Dpldsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores powered by the Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor operating at 3.4 GHz. The server is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core ratio. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 1890 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark results show strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 25% tier. Memory performance is a key strength, with large-block read-only memory bandwidth and PassMark memory scores reaching the top 10% tier. Database operations also perform in the top 10% tier. However, single-core performance and large LLM inference tasks, such as prompt processing for 70B models, show average to poor performance, indicating a tradeoff where parallelized workloads are favored over raw single-threaded speed.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture and lower memory-to-core ratio offer a resource-dense configuration for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. This server is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, database operations, static web serving, and software compilation. It is less optimal for memory-intensive databases or large-scale AI model inference.
